topic: Dynamic Memory Reallocation with realloc() for Growing Data Structures
explanation: In advanced C programming, managing dynamic data structures efficiently requires the ability to resize memory blocks at runtime without losing existing data. The realloc() function enables developers to expand or shrink previously allocated memory, facilitating the implementation of flexible, growable tables or buffers. Proper use of realloc() involves careful checking of its return value to avoid memory leaks or dangling pointers, making it a critical technique for high-performance, memory-efficient applications that need to adapt to varying data sizes during execution.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates advanced use of realloc() to dynamically grow a character array (table) as new elements are added. When the current number of elements reaches the allocated capacity, realloc() is called to double the size of the memory block, preserving existing data. The code carefully checks the return value of realloc() to handle potential failures, exemplifying best practices in advanced memory management. This technique allows the data structure to scale efficiently during runtime, a common requirement in high-performance or memory-constrained applications.
